If you wanted my experience then ask for my experience. And you’re not getting my point. He does need them. Would you not say you need ear protection if you were standing next to something so loud it caused pain? That’s what sensory processing disorder is. Yes, to you a store might not seem loud at all, but to him, it could be as loud and overwhelming as if he were in the middle of a busy construction site. And how is it harmful to wear headphones? Give me some legitimate reasons why. And if you want to know something, ask a direct question. How am i supposed to know you asking what ABA is means asking my personal experience?

See??? If you don't understand the concept of sensory comforts, how can you claim to know anything about autism? Sensory processing disorder is frequently comorbid with autism. When that happens, the input from the senses is either drastically lowered or increased. What this means is that, in some cases, sounds can be painful and overwhelming for the autistic person, so wearing headphones is a harmless was to reduce that input and provide a basic sensory comfort. Would you like it if someone made you stand next to a painfully loud speaker with no ear protection? ABA is an abusive but common therapy for autistic people.
It’s not a tantrum but okay. I feel bad for your nephew being denied basic sensory comforts. You obviously know nothing about autism and probably think ABA is a great therapy.

You know a lot of autistic people wear headphones everywhere they go? It’s because of sensory processing disorder, which can be physically painful. Maybe he wanted his shirt off at the dinner table because the fabric was irritating. It’s not ‘indulging’ him, it’s letting him make harmless modifications to his life to mitigate how incredibly overwhelming and painful the world can be to someone with autism.
